FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 March 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 

Wooden loop handles are used with two-men cross cut saws for felling and cross cutting of trees of 
diameter more than 200 mm. These handles have advantage over the traditionally used permanent 
fixed clamps as the saw blades can be taken out from the kerf even after fixing the wedges in the kerf 
by the use of handles. 

The requirements for single grip reversible handles used with two-men cross cut saws are specified in 
IS 12128 ; 1987 'Specification for reversible handles for cross cut saws'. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the Forest Operations Division, 
Forest Research Institute ( ICFR ), Dehra Dun. 

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, 
observed or calculated is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for 
rounding off numerical values ( revised )'. 



IS 12627 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — LOOP HANDLES, TWO- 
MEN CROSS CUT SAWS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the material, dimen- 
sions and other requirements for loop handles for 
two-men cross cut saws in accordance with IS 
12127 : 1987 'Specification for two-men cross cut 
saws*. 



2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The Indian Standards given 
necessary adjuncts to this standard; 



below are

3 MATERUL 

3.1 Handles 

The handles shall be made from good quality, 
seasoned hard wood, such as. Acacia arabica 
( Babul ), Acacia catechu ( Khair ), Anogeissus 
latifolia ( Bakli ), Adina CordifoUa ( Haldu ), 
Azadirecta indica ( Neem ), Ougeinia dalbergioides 
( Sandan ), Schleichera trijuga ( Kusum ), Shorea 
robusta ( Sal ), Terminalia tomentosa ( Laurel ), 
etc. 

3.1.1 Wooden blanks shall be free from centre 
lieart ( pith ), decay ( rot ), checks, shakes, splits, 
borer holes, warp, etc. 

3.2 Cap, Washer and Nut 

Shall be made from mild steel ( see IS 226 : 1975 ). 



3.3 Loop Bolt 

Shall be made from spring steel (see IS 2507 : 
1975 ). 

4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

4.1 The shape and dimensions shall be as shown 
in Fig. lA to IC. 

4.1.1 Tolerance for the dimensions shall l)e of 
very coarse class specified in IS 2102 ( Part 1 ) : 
1980. 

5 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 It is recommended that immediately after 
manufacture, the handles shall be dipped in raw 
linseed oil at about 90^C for one hour. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 There shall be no play in the loop bolt after 
tightening with the nut. Forgings shall be free 
from burrs, pits, sharp edges, cracks and other 
defects. 

6.2 Threads shall be well formed. 

7 DESIGNATION 

7.1 Loop handles shall be designated by its name 
and the number of this Indian Standard as: 

Loop Handle IS 12627 

8 MARKING 

8.1 Each handle shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark, if any, and the batch or code number. 

9 PACKING 

9.1 The packing shall be done as agreed to 
between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

10 SAMPLING 

10.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier, the sampling plan 
and criteria for conformity shall be as given in 
Annex A.

ANNEX A 

( Clause 10.1 ) 

SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 



A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
A-1.1 Lot 

In any consignment, all the handles of the same 
nominal size manufactured under similar condi- 
tions of manufacture shall be grouped together 
to constitute a lot. 

A-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot 
to the requirements of this specification, tests 
shall be carried out from the handles selected from 
each lot separately. The number jof handles to 
be selected at random from a lot shall be in 
accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. To ensure 
the randomness of selection, the procedure as laid 
down in IS 4905 : 1968 may be followed. 

A-2 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA 
FOR CONFORMITY 

A-2.1 The handles selected according to A-i.2 
shall be examined for material ( see 3 ), dimensions 
( see 4 ), and general requirements ( see 5 ). Any 
handle failing to meet the requirements for any 



one or more of the characteristics mentioned 
above shall be declared defective. 

A-2.1.1 The lot shall be considered conforming to 
the requirements of the characteristics mentioned 
above if the number of handles found defective is 
less than or equal to the corresponding number 
given in col 3 of Table 1 . 

Table 1 Sampling Size and Permissible 
Number of Defectives 

( Clauses A-1.2 and A-2.1. 1 )

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau, of Indiqn 
Standards Act, 1986 and the^ules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on , 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of irispection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operate4 by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS.
